title: Bounded serial autonomy from intent to verified delivery
outcomes: Turn authorized intent into grounded executable tasks connected to vision, architecture and original outcomes.
Continue serially through repair, independent task releases and recovery without manual per-task dispatch.
Prove actual bounded user goals and provide auditable delivery readback.

in: Task exploration and semantic readiness, bounded campaign contract/controller, recovery/budgets, behavioral evidence and goal audit, serial release/cleanup, deterministic and live campaign proof
out: Parallel builders, inter-worker messaging bus, multi-host scheduling, new provider/session adapters, unbounded feature discovery and GitHub Actions
systems: go-project-template through its own follow-up task
boundaries: Existing canonical .go remains the workflow authority; task/run/workspace/release records remain authoritative within one host and one writer at a time.

concerns: Original agreements and useful live results
decision_rights: Authorize goal, bounded delegation, budget and actual publication targets; current request authorizes task creation only

concerns: No duplicate state or ceremonial architecture
decision_rights: Resolve bounded implementation choices using existing accepted architecture; never fabricate human approval

constraints: Reuse existing ABC, R# outcomes, architecture decision/conformance gates and v0.3.33 readiness; implement deltas rather than duplicate systems.
Broad vision guides relevance but does not authorize new work; research and repair expansion must fit the adopted goal.
Make authority explicit and preserve prior user delegation; conditional architecture gates apply only where relevant.
Keep final proof tied to the tested candidate and observed release; preparation is not product completion.
One worker, durable task/project binding and cumulative budget; resume checks actual process and external-effect state.
The versioned campaign contract bounds execution authority; dependent runtime tasks must preserve its explicit allowlist, cumulative budget, unresolved decisions and separate delivery grants.

quality_attributes.scenario: A rough multi-part request is explored, split, repaired and delivered
quality_attributes.measure: Original adopted outcomes lost or falsely verified

quality_attributes.scenario: Three eligible serial tasks with adequate budget
quality_attributes.measure: User prompts needed solely to dispatch the next task

quality_attributes.scenario: Controller/process interruption or lost publication acknowledgement
quality_attributes.measure: Duplicate writers, repeated unobserved external effects or erased work

quality_attributes.scenario: Queue empty but behavioral evidence missing

quality_attributes.measure: Task reported delivered without required fresh release/live proof

risks: Semantic task/readiness/goal judgement requires grounded review; JSON shape or deterministic fixtures cannot prove model quality.
Existing architecture classification may identify foundational changes; inspect real scope and existing human authority before execution, never infer approval from intake.
Pilot setup, runtime availability and live provider limits can block live proof even with green deterministic tests.
open_questions: autonomy-09 requires a concrete authorized pilot project, profiles, budget and delivery destination; Hearthhold is not implicitly authorized.
